title: 660-28 engine no-crank: battery, starter feed, ground and interlocks

steps.instruction: Move the unit to an approved service position, apply the parking brake and chock the wheels. With the required operator controls in their normal start positions, command START once and observe the starter without holding the key. Confirm whether this is a no-crank complaint rather than an engine that cranks but does not start.
steps.question: Does the starter remain stationary and fail to rotate the engine when START is commanded?

steps.instruction: Before meter work, verify the normal starting state against the operator manual: transmission selector actually in neutral, parking brake applied, seat/operator-presence conditions met, emergency stop reset where applicable, and no active start-inhibit indication. Do not jumper any interlock.
steps.question: Are all required operator and interlock conditions genuinely satisfied, with control positions and indications agreeing?

steps.instruction: Switch off and inspect the starting-battery case, hold-down, posts, clamps, main power lead, engine ground strap and accessible starter connections. Look for looseness, corrosion, broken strands, heat damage and evidence of previous jump-start polarity damage. Do not make repairs until the required electrical isolation is complete.
steps.question: Are the battery and accessible power/ground connections physically serviceable and secure?

steps.instruction: Measure and record open-circuit voltage directly across the starting-battery posts using a DVOM. Compare only with the battery/equipment manufacturer's resting-voltage criterion for the actual battery type and condition; nominal system voltage is not an acceptance range. If an approved criterion is not available, stop and obtain it rather than guessing pass/fail.
steps.question: Does the recorded resting voltage meet the applicable manual criterion?

steps.instruction: Keep the DVOM across the battery posts. Have an assistant make a normal START command while all required interlocks remain functional, and record the minimum stable cranking voltage. Do not extend cranking to obtain a number. Compare with the manual's cranking-voltage and duration requirements.
steps.question: Does battery voltage during cranking remain within the applicable manual acceptance range?

steps.instruction: Measure voltage drop from the battery positive lead post to the starter main B+ stud during cranking. Use the complete feed first; if excessive, repeat segment by segment to locate the cable, lug, connection or contact causing the drop. Keep leads clear of hot and rotating parts.
steps.question: Is the positive-feed voltage drop within the maximum allowed by the applicable manual?

steps.instruction: Move the meter to measure ground-side voltage drop from the starter housing/designated starter ground to the battery negative lead post during cranking. Test the whole return path first and then the engine-to-chassis and chassis-to-battery segments if needed.
steps.question: Is the ground-side voltage drop within the maximum allowed by the applicable manual?

steps.instruction: With the main feed and ground demonstrated good, back-probe the starter solenoid S/control terminal to battery negative during a normal START command. Note both measured voltage and whether the solenoid clicks. Do not short the adjacent B+ terminal and do not bypass the control circuit.
steps.question: Is the solenoid control-terminal voltage within the applicable manual range while START is commanded?

steps.instruction: Isolate the machine before any mechanical inspection or component removal.
steps.terminal_result: Main feed, ground and solenoid control are good but the original no-crank remains. Suspect the starter solenoid/motor or mechanical engine drag/lock. First verify by the manufacturer method that the engine is free to rotate with ignition/fuel safely disabled and electrical energy isolated, then bench-test or replace the starter only if that test and inspection support it. Retest cranking after repair.

steps.instruction: Trace the start-control circuit using the applicable wiring diagram. With the selector verified in neutral and START commanded, back-probe the neutral-start switch output to battery negative without jumpering the switch. Inspect the connector and mechanical selector alignment while taking the reading.
steps.question: Is neutral-start switch output voltage present within the applicable manual range?

steps.instruction: Leave the safety interlocks functional and isolate the circuit before connector repair.
steps.terminal_result: Neutral-start output is present but the starter S terminal did not receive an acceptable control signal. Isolate the downstream open or high resistance between this switch and the solenoid: inspect the identified connectors, start relay or other series devices shown on the actual schematic, and repair wiring/connections or replace only a component proven faulty. Restore all interlocks and retest start/inhibit operation.

steps.instruction: Return the selector and controls to their normal positions and isolate before adjustment.
steps.terminal_result: Neutral-start output is absent or low. Verify real transmission neutral, selector linkage alignment and supply to the switch, then test the neutral-start switch and upstream start-command path against the wiring diagram. Adjust or replace only the item proven faulty; never defeat the neutral safety function. Confirm start occurs only in permitted selector positions after repair.

steps.instruction: Record the actual cranking and starting behavior before choosing another diagnostic path.
steps.terminal_result: This is not a no-crank fault. If the engine rotates but fails to start, leave this tree and diagnose cranking speed, fuel and ignition/combustion using the Ford engine and equipment procedures; check for a fuel leak before further cranking. A crank-no-start decision tree has not yet been seeded in this package.

steps.instruction: Do not continue to starter replacement until the normal start state can be achieved.
steps.terminal_result: Correct the operator setup and confirm whether cranking is restored. If physical control positions and their indications disagree, inspect the related seat/presence, parking-brake, neutral or emergency-stop switch, connector and linkage using the applicable schematic and adjustment procedure. Do not bypass an interlock; verify both permitted starting and prohibited starting states after repair.

steps.instruction: Isolate the battery before cleaning, tightening or replacing any high-current connection.
steps.terminal_result: Repair the identified visual/connection defect first: clean and protect serviceable battery connections, replace damaged leads to the specified routing and terminal practice, secure the battery, or replace a battery with case/terminal damage after confirming specifications. Repeat the complete connection inspection and resting/cranking voltage tests rather than installing a starter as the first repair.

steps.instruction: Identify the battery type before selecting a charger or charging profile.
steps.terminal_result: Resting voltage does not support a valid starter test. Charge the correct battery type by the approved method, then repeat resting voltage and an approved battery load/capacity test. If the battery passes, investigate charging performance and parasitic draw; if it fails, replace it with the specified type and recheck the starting circuit. Do not interpret a discharged battery alone as proof of an internally defective battery.

steps.instruction: Stop repeated start attempts while the low-voltage cause is unresolved.
steps.terminal_result: Battery voltage falls below the manual criterion under cranking load. Recharge and perform the approved battery load/capacity test, clean and secure connections, and check for abnormal starter current or mechanical drag if the battery is good. Do not condemn the starter until battery condition and cable loss have been separated from excessive starter/engine load.

steps.instruction: Isolate before disturbing the positive high-current feed.
steps.terminal_result: Excessive starter positive-feed voltage drop localizes unwanted resistance in the positive cable path. Compare segment drops to isolate the battery post/clamp, cable, lug, connector or series solenoid/contact, then clean, repair or replace only the defective section with correctly rated parts. Repeat the loaded voltage-drop test and confirm the repaired lead does not overheat.

steps.instruction: Isolate before removing ground straps or cleaning mating surfaces.
steps.terminal_result: Excessive ground-side voltage drop localizes resistance in the starter/engine/chassis/battery-negative return. Use segment tests to find the defective housing bond, engine strap, chassis connection, negative cable or clamp; repair the connection to clean, secure metal and replace damaged cable. Retest ground drop under load before evaluating the starter.

title: 600i Power Stow no lift or slow lift: supply, pressure, relief, cylinder and flow

steps.instruction: Remove baggage and other load. Move to an approved service area, park on level ground, apply the parking brake and chock the wheels. Inspect the loading head, conveyor, lift arms, hoses and cylinders for impact damage, obstruction, obvious external leakage or a person/tool in the travel path. Lower and mechanically support raised equipment before close inspection.
steps.question: Is the machine clear, unloaded and mechanically safe for a controlled hydraulic function test?

steps.instruction: With the lift in the manual-required checking position and pressure isolated, inspect reservoir level, fluid identity and condition, filler/breather and visible inlet hose. Look for aeration, milky contamination, debris and a collapsed or leaking suction line. Use only fluid allowed by the correct manual if correction is needed.
steps.question: Are oil level and condition correct and the visible pump inlet path free of obvious restriction or air entry?

steps.instruction: Test each Power Stow 12 V battery individually with a DVOM, then repeat using the manual-approved hydraulic load condition. Identify and preserve correct series connections. Record every reading rather than judging only total bank voltage; compare with the actual battery and equipment criteria before continuing.
steps.question: Does each auxiliary battery meet the applicable resting and loaded voltage criteria during the lift-pump supply test?

steps.instruction: Only after verifying the manufacturer test-port ID and full procedure, connect a rated gauge at the Power Stow main lift-pump outlet with energy isolated. Re-energize for the documented normal lift command and record pressure, oil temperature and pump-drive behavior. Do not hold at relief or deadhead a circuit unless explicitly instructed by the manual. Stop and escalate if the exact procedure/range is unavailable.
steps.question: Is the measured main lift pressure within the manual range for the prescribed lift test?

steps.instruction: With normal supply pressure demonstrated, use the manufacturer-provided cap-end pressure connection and supported loading-head procedure to determine whether pressure reaches the lift cylinder. Do not loosen a cylinder hose to improvise a test point. Keep personnel and leads outside the loading-head travel path.
steps.question: Does cap-end cylinder pressure meet the manual range and show that commanded pressure reaches the cylinder?

steps.instruction: Maintain the specified mechanical support and use the manufacturer-approved rod-end/return connection. Perform only the prescribed lift or hold test and record rod-end pressure/back-pressure to assess return restriction, check/counterbalance operation and possible cylinder internal leakage.
steps.question: Is rod-end/back-pressure within the manual range for the prescribed lift or hold test?

steps.instruction: Because main pressure was low, test the main relief valve only by the manufacturer relief-setting and isolation procedure. Check for contamination, premature opening, incorrect setting and unrestricted bypass. Do not turn an adjustment blindly and do not mask low pressure with a higher relief setting.
steps.question: Does the relief valve hold and open at the correct manual setting without evidence of premature bypass?

steps.instruction: With relief operation verified, have a qualified technician install the rated inline flow/pressure test set and measure pump delivery at the manufacturer-defined load, oil temperature and pump-drive condition. Record pressure and flow together; do not close the test-set load valve without a documented limit.
steps.question: Is pump delivery flow within the manual range under the prescribed load and operating conditions?

steps.instruction: Isolate and support before inspecting the cylinder feed path.
steps.terminal_result: Main pump pressure is available but does not reach the cylinder cap end correctly. Use the hydraulic schematic to isolate the loading-head control solenoid/spool, electrical command, obstructed line/hose and pilot-operated check valve. Verify command power and mechanical spool movement before replacing the cylinder; repair the proven restriction or control fault and repeat the supported functional test.

steps.instruction: Keep the loading head mechanically supported throughout mechanical inspection.
steps.terminal_result: Available cylinder pressures do not explain the no/slow movement, so inspect for mechanical binding, bent lift arms or cylinder rod, damaged pivots/slides, foreign-object obstruction and incorrect auto-level geometry. Unload the mechanism before checking free movement by the manufacturer method. If the mechanism moves freely and all readings genuinely meet specification, repeat the functional test with an approved loaded procedure rather than replacing parts.

steps.instruction: Isolate and support before separating any return or cylinder component.
steps.terminal_result: Abnormal rod-end/back-pressure indicates a return/check/counterbalance restriction or cylinder internal-bypass problem. Isolate these possibilities with the manufacturer pressure/hold test: inspect the return path and correct valve operation first, then evaluate cylinder seal leakage only after external causes are excluded. Correct any contamination source before returning the repaired circuit to service.

steps.instruction: Depressurize and isolate before removing or adjusting a relief valve.
steps.terminal_result: The relief valve is opening prematurely, bypassing, contaminated or incorrectly set. Follow the manufacturer clean/inspect/replace and adjustment procedure; find the cause of contamination or overheating rather than repeatedly resetting the valve. Adjust only to the cited specification with a calibrated gauge, lock the setting as directed and verify normal lift without increasing pressure beyond the manual limit.

steps.instruction: Recheck the test configuration before selecting replacement parts.
steps.terminal_result: Measured delivery is acceptable although the earlier main-pressure result was low. This is not proof of a defective pump: verify the flow/pressure test points and conditions, then isolate an unintended bypass through the relief/control circuit or an incorrect test configuration using the schematic. Repeat the pressure-versus-flow check and continue to the cylinder/valve branch only when readings are repeatable.

steps.instruction: Isolate electrical and hydraulic energy before pump or inlet service.
steps.terminal_result: Low pump delivery is confirmed. Check pump drive-motor voltage under load, connector drop, contactor/relay operation and actual motor speed first; then inspect reservoir supply, inlet hose and suction restriction for air entry or collapse. Replace the pump only after drive and inlet causes are excluded or pump testing proves wear/damage. Correct oil contamination and verify pressure and flow after repair.

steps.instruction: Tag the unit out of service until the observed hazard is corrected.
steps.terminal_result: Do not run a hydraulic function test with a person or tool in the travel path, aircraft conflict, damaged lift structure, obstructed mechanism or active external leak. Clear the area, secure and support the equipment, and repair structural/hose/cylinder damage under the manufacturer procedure. Restart this tree only after the unsafe condition is eliminated.

steps.instruction: Resolve fluid loss or contamination before further loaded testing.
steps.terminal_result: Correct low/incorrect/contaminated fluid or the visible inlet defect with the exact approved fluid and service procedure. Locate and repair the source of oil loss, aeration or water/debris entry; replace a restricted or collapsing inlet hose as indicated. Simply topping off is not a permanent repair. Check for pump damage after severe cavitation, then repeat this tree from the safe inspection.

steps.instruction: Identify the correct battery type and series configuration before charging or replacement.
steps.terminal_result: Auxiliary battery supply does not support the hydraulic pump load. Charge and test each battery by the approved method, inspect high-current cables and grounds for voltage drop, and verify charger operation. Replace weak batteries only to specification and in the matched manner required by the Power Stow maintenance manual. Repeat the loaded supply test before condemning the pump, relief valve or cylinder.
